doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: Accompanying singers and working with Joe Williams
summary: He lists singers he accompanied, then describes the easy gigs with Joe Williams and the need to know tunes in any key.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Interesting. You have accompanied along the way some great singers, too.
Yeah, I’ve been with Lena Horne, Dinah Washington, Kay Starr, I even was with Dinah Shore one night. And let’s see who else. So many I forget most of them, yeah.
Did you ever cross paths with Joe Williams?
Oh, I see Joe all the time. Every time he comes to L.A. he usually hired my trio, yeah. His piano player doesn’t want to make the trip out here so I get the job, which is great for me.
What’s it like working with Joe?

Easiest job on earth. But I don’t have to play his regular stuff. You know when he works with his piano player, they have all this stuff set up. But when he comes out here he says, “Wig, don’t worry about it.” The blues. We do the blues in any — all kind of keys. We do a ballad now and then, but it’s very easy working for him.
That’s interesting. You know the non-jazz musician always finds it fascinating when if you watch someone and they say B flat, and that’s all the band needs. You know, that’s one great thing about —
Well you’re supposed to know the tunes, you know?

That’s another thing — for this type of festival, too, when you watch the bands up there, and you’ve really got to have a repertory in your head of tunes. Because some of them aren’t groups that work together all the time, so someone turns around and says, you know, this particular tune—
In E flat, and you better know it.
Yeah. Any key they call you’re supposed to be able to play it.
